title: WPSB/550/2017 of KANHAIYA JI MISHRA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COMMON JUDGMENT : (per Hon'ble The Chief Justice Ms. Ritu Bahri)
This order shall dispose of above mentioned 07
cases, as common questions of facts and law are involved
in them.
2. By means of the present Writ Petitions, the
petitioners are challenging the judgment and order dated
07.11.2017 passed by the Uttarakhand Public Services
Tribunal, Bench at Nainital, whereby the Claim Petition of
private contesting respondents, i.e. Claim Petition No.
01/NB/DB/2015, has been allowed, and the final seniority
list issued on 03.01.2015, as well as the select list/

4
recommendations of the DPC dated 04.01.2015, and the
promotion letter/ order dated 05.01.2015, whereby the
proforma respondents were promoted to the post of
Executive Engineer, have been quashed, and set-aside.
Further, the Tribunal directed the respondent in said
Claim Petition to prepare a fresh seniority list according
to the Rules and Regulations, and as per the observations
made by the Tribunal by treating the appointment of the
respondents (direct recruits) from the date of their
substantive appointment to the cadre, after completion of
their training period for the purpose of seniority.
3. The brief facts are that the U.P. State Electricity
Board, in order to provide and regulate the recruitment
and service conditions of the Assistant Engineers, framed
and enforced 'the Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Board
Services of Engineers Regulations, 1970' (hereinafter to
be referred as "the 1970 Regulations"). The 1970
Regulations stood amended, to the extent of repugnancy
only, by Regulations, namely U.P. State Electricity Board
Servants' Seniority Regulations, 1998, which were issued
by the U.P. State Electricity Board.

5
4. Thereafter, the State of Uttarakhand was
created on 09th November 2000. Consequent upon the
creation of the State, Uttaranchal Power Corporation Ltd.
(now renamed as "Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd.)
(hereinafter to be referred as "UPCL"), was incorporated
under the Companies Act, 1956 on February 12, 2001.
UPCL has been entrusted to cater to the Transmission &
Distribution Sectors inherited after the de-merger from
U.P. Power Corporation Ltd., the erstwhile U.P.S.E.B since
01st April 2001. The Electricity Act, 2003 mandated the
separation of Transmission functions under Power Sector
Reforms. On 1st June 2004, the Power Transmission
Corporation Limited (PTCUL) was formed to maintain &
operate 132 KV & above Transmission Lines & substations
in the State, and is a separate entity.
5. On 01.10.2006, UPCL issued an advertisement
in all leading newspapers, inviting applications from
eligible persons, for appointment to the post of Assistant
Engineer (E&M). The upper age limit for applying,
pursuant to the said advertisement, was 40 years as on
01.07.2006. By the said advertisement 37 vacancies of
Assistant Engineer (E&M) were advertised. The

6
advertised vacancies were for the recruitment year 2006-
07.
6. Respondent nos. 10 to 35 possess B.E. and
B.Tech. degree, therefore, they all were eligible for
appointment to the post of Assistant Engineer (E&M), as
per the advertisement. After short-listing, admit cards
were issued to eligible candidates, and on the strength of
such admit cards, the proforma private respondents
participated in the written examination, which was held
on 31.12.2006. Those candidates, who qualified the
written examination, were called for interview, and all the
proforma respondents appeared before the Interview
Board. On the recommendation of the Selection
Committee, the competent authority appointed
respondent nos. 10 to 29 as Assistant Engineer (E&M) for
the selection year 2007-08. Pursuant to issuance of the
appointment letters, respondent nos. 10 to 29 joined
their duties as Assistant Engineer (Trainee) in UPCL up to
June 2008. Respondent nos. 30 to 33 joined on the post
of Assistant Engineer (Trainee) up to December 2008.
The appointment letter was issued to the respondents
nos. 34 and 35 in February, 2009. Respondents no. 34

7
joined in May, 2009 and respondent no. 35 joined in
April, 2009 respectively at UPCL on their respective posts.
7. After examination, a list, in the order of merit,
was prepared, and the successful candidates were offered
to join as Assistant Engineer (Trainee). Here, it is
relevant to state that the list of the successful candidates,
so prepared, contained names of those candidates also,
who were offered appointment, and were recruited, after
the candidates placed at higher position in the list had not
joined as Assistant Engineer (Trainee). It is worthwhile
to mention that such candidates, who were in waiting-list,
were offered appointment on the posts within one year
from the date of publication of the result of the
examination of recruitment process.
8. Thereafter, the petitioners in the Claim Petition
were promoted on the post of Assistant Engineer
(Electrical & Mechanical) in the year 2007-08 & 2008-09.
The other private respondents were appointed on the
post of Assistant Engineer in the year 2008-09, after
selection and completion of training against the vacancies
of 2006-07. The respondent-department issued a
combined seniority list of the cadre of Assistant Engineers

8
(Electrical & Mechanical), in which respondents nos. 3 to
22 were given seniority right from the date when they
joined the services as Trainee after their selection on the
basis of advertisement. The petitioners in the claim
petition have challenged their seniority on the ground
that their substantive appointment cannot be treated
from the date of their induction as Trainees, but from the
date of their substantive appointment in the cadre by the
department, after completion of their training.
9. The Uttarakhand Public Services Tribunal has
allowed the Claim Petition, and had set-aside the
seniority list issued on 03.01.2015, and recommendation
of the DPC dated 04.01.2015, and the promotion letter/
order dated 05.01.2015, whereby the directly recruited
Assistant Engineers have been given promotion on the
post of Executive Engineer by treating them senior from
the date of their joining the department. The Tribunal
has held that these directly recruited Assistant Engineers
can be given seniority from the date they have finished
their training, and not from the date they joined after
regular selection process.
10. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

9
11. Counsel for the petitioners in the present case
has argued that the State of Uttarakhand was created on
09.11.2000, and, thereafter, Uttaranchal Power
Corporation Ltd., now renamed as Uttarakhand Power
Corporation Ltd., was incorporated under the Companies
Act, 1956 on 12.02.2001. It is their specific case that for
the purpose of regulating the recruitment and service
conditions, the State of Uttarakhand has adopted the
Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Board Services of
Engineers Regulations, 1970, which were subsequently
amended by Regulations, namely U.P. State Electricity
Board Servant Seniority Regulations 1998 issued by the
U.P. State Electricity Board. Hence, for the purpose of
recruitment and seniority, the above-said Regulations are
being applied till date, and reference can now be made to
the above-said Regulations, with respect to seniority.
12. Reference again can be made to the
Notification (Annexure No. 4) dated 31.03.2001 issued by
the Managing Director of the Corporation, after creation
of the State of Uttarakhand, wherein it is stated that till
new Regulations are formulated, they will follow the Uttar
Pradesh Power Corporation Regulations. This notification

10
has been issued until the new Regulations are made after
the creation of the State of Uttarakhand, and the
Regulations of the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation shall
be followed till then. Subsequently, another notification
has also been placed on record by the Uttaranchal Power
Corporation Ltd. - Annexure No. 5 dated 05.12.2001,
whereby it has been clarified that no Rules and
Regulations of the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation
enforced after 01.11.2001 will be applicable unless and
until such Rules and Regulations are made applicable by
the Corporation.
13. A reading of both the office memorandums
dated 31.03.2001 - Annexure No. 4 and 05.12.2001 -
Annexure No. 5 makes it abundantly clear that initially,
vide office memorandum dated 31.03.2001 - Annexure
No. 4, a conscious decision has been taken that unless
new Regulations are framed the old Regulations of the
U.P. Power Corporation will be applicable, and since this
letter had already been issued, then as per the office
memorandum dated 05.12.2001, it has again been said
that the U.P. Power Corporation Regulations will not be
enforced unless and until they are made applicable by the
Corporation, and the Office Memorandum dated

11
31.03.2001 - Annexure No. 4 has been issued, and would
be applicable till the new Regulations are made by the
Uttarakhand Power Corporation. Till date, no new
Regulations have been framed with regard to
recruitment, and seniority of the employees of the
Uttarakhand Power Corporation.
14. Hence, taking the office memorandum dated
31.03.2001 - Annexure No. 4 issued by the Managing
Director for all intents and purposes, the rule of seniority,
as per the 1970 Regulations, amended in 1998, have to
be applied. The moment new Regulations come, the UP
Regulations will not be applicable.
15. Now for the purpose of regulating
determination of seniority, as per the provisions of 1970
Regulations and 1998 Regulations, the rule of seniority,
as per 1970 regulations is as under. For the purpose of
these Writ Petitions, Rule 19 deals with seniority, which
reads as under:
"19. Seniority.
The seniority of officers on their appointment to
the service shall be determined according to the date of
the order of appointment to a particular post in the
cadres of the service;
Provided firstly that if two or more candidates are
appointed on the same date, their seniority inter se
shall be determined according to the order in which

12
their names appear in the orders of appointment issued
by the Appointing Authority, or in other words, the
order in which their names are placed in the 'Select
List' or 'Combined Waiting List', as the case may be;
Provided secondly that the Appointing Authority
may direct that an officer whose period of probation is
extended for failure to prove his fitness for confirmation
be placed in the seniority list next below the last
confirmed member;
Provided thirdly that the relative seniority of
members of the Service who are appointed by direct
recruitment shall be in accordance with the order of
preference in which they are placed by the Selection
Committee at the time of selection, as approved by the
Appointing Authority;
Provided fourthly that as between candidates who
are appointed by direct recruitment and who are
recruited by promotion in the same year, the seniority
shall be determined in the order in which their names
are arranged in the combined waiting list prepared
under Regulation 15, provided that if in any year, it has
not been possible to prepare the combined waiting list
due to late selection either from Junior Engineers
Service or from Computers (Selection Grade) or found
outside or due to any other unavoidable reasons, the
names in the gradation list shall be arranged in the
same order in due course in respect of the vacancies
allotted to each of the categories of candidates in that
particular year, as in the combined waiting list and the
seniority determined accordingly;
Provided fifthly, that the inter se seniority of
Government Officers absorbed in the service of the
Board, while officiating in any cadre of the Board's
service, shall be the same as on the post held by them
in the Government in a permanent/substantive capacity
and in the case of those officers who were not
permanent on any post at the time of absorption shall
be the same as on the lower post held by them after
regular selection in an officiating capacity."
16. As far as the recruitment made in the year
2007-08 & 2008-09 of the Assistant Engineers is
concerned, nobody is disputing the fact that the process
of selection was made as per the advertisement, and

13
appointment was made as per the merit list prepared by
the Recruitment Agency. With respect to fixation of
seniority, Rule 19 is to be applied, and as per Rule 19,
referred to above, the seniority of the officers has to be
determined as per the date of order of appointment to a
particular post in the cadre of the service. Hence, for all
intents and purposes, after selection, when the Assistant
Engineers joined the post to the cadre of the service,
their seniority has to be determined from that date, and
after joining if they are sent on training, that period is to
be taken as part of their service after joining.
17. Similar is the provision of Rule 8 of the
Regulations of 1998 relating to seniority, which is
reproduced as under :-
"8. In that condition seniority should be
determined when appointments are made
from promotions and direct recruitment.
(1) Where according to the service regulations
appointments, promotion and direct recruitment
are to be done in both the ways, at that place the
seniority of the persons appointed in this way will
be determined under the provisions of the
following sub Rule from the date of order of their
basic appointment and if two or more persons are
appointed together, then in that sequence it will
be determined, in which their names have been
kept in the order of appointment.
Restriction is this that if in the order of
appointment any such specific prior date is
specified by which any person is appointed
basically, then when that date will be considered
as the date of appointment, the date or order of

14
the basic appointment and in other matters its
meaning will be date of issuing order.
The further restriction is this that any
candidate recruited directly may lose his seniority
if on the proposal of any vacant post given to
him, he fails in assuming charge without legal
reasons. Regarding the legal acceptance of the
reasons, the decision of the appointing authority
will be final.
(2) Due to any one selection:
(a) The inter se seniority of persons
appointed directly will be the same as
it has been shown in the merit list
prepared by the commission of
committee as it is.
(b) The inter se-seniority of the
appointment persons by promotion
will be the same which according to
this situation that the promotion is
done from the single feeder cadre or
from many feeder cadres. According
to the principles given in the
regulation 6 or regulation 7, as it is,
may be determined.
(3) Where due to any selection the
appointments are made in both the ways by
promotion and by direct recruitment, at that
place seniority of the promoted persons vis-à-vis
a seniority of the persons recruited directly, so
far it is possible according to the prescribed quota
for both the sources in sequence of turns. Place
will be of the promoted persons will be
determined.
As for example -
(1) Where there is a quota of promoted
persons and of the persons directly recruited is in
the proportion of 1:1 at that place the seniority
will of the following sequence :-
1st - promoted person
2nd - the person directly
recruited and in this way
further also

15
(2) Where the said quota is in proportion of 1:3
at that place the seniority will be in the following
sequence :-
1st - Promoted person
2nd to 4th - persons directly appointed
5th - promoted persons
6th to 8th - directly recruited persons
and this way further also
Restriction is that :-
(1) Where from any source appointment are
made more than the prescribed quota, at
that place for the seniority of the persons
appointed more than the quota for those
subsequent year or years will be increased,
in which are vacancies according to quota.
(2) Where the appointments from any source
are less than the prescribed quota and
against such unfilled vacancies, the
appointments are made in the subsequent
year or years then the persons appointed in
this way will not get seniority of any
previous years but they will get seniority of
that year, in which their appointments are
made, but their names will be kept at the
top, after which the names of other
appointed persons will be kept in sequence
of turn.
(3) Where according to the service Regulations
in the circumstance mentioned in the
relevant service regulations, the vacancies
without being filled from any source may be
filled from other source and appointments
should be made more than the quota, at
that place the person appointed in this way
will get the seniority of that every year as if
they are appointed against the vacancies of
their quota."
18. At this stage, the only dispute in the present
case is with respect to the seniority, whether the period
of training is to be counted as part of service. This issue
has already come up before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in

16
Union of India and others etc. v. S.D. Gupta and
others, AIR 1996 SC 3325. In the said case, the
Hon'ble Supreme Court was examining the question of
seniority of direct recruits vis-à-vis the promotees. As far
as the direct recruits were concerned, the Hon'ble
Supreme Court observed that even if a person is
appointed by way of direct recruitment on ad hoc basis,
he will be confirmed after probation, however, he
becomes part of the service cadre on the date of his
initial appointment, and if a promotee is given promotion
on the basis of rota quota of vacancies, where in a cadre
40% quota is to be filled by promotees, and 60% quota
by way of direct recruits, the promotees, who are given
promotion against their quota post, cannot be made
junior to a direct recruit, even if the vacancy of direct
recruit arose before their promotion. The direct recruit
becomes part of the cadre only after appointment.
19. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, thereafter, in the
year 2021 in the case of Muzeeb Burrahman & Ors. v.
U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors., (Civil Appeal
Nos. 5646-5647 of 2021) was examining the same
Regulations of 1970 & 1998. While examining the U.P.
Power Corporation Regulations, which are relevant in the

17
present case also, the Supreme Court held that a person
appointed against a clear substantive vacancy in the
direct recruit quota can legitimately claim to be born in
the cadre from the date of his initial appointment and not
after completion of training or probation. The Hon'ble
Supreme Court observed as under :
"This Court is of the opinion that the conclusions
recorded by the High Court reflect the correct position
of the Rules. A person appointed against a clear
substantive vacancy in the direct recruit quota, under
the existing Rules, can legitimately claim to be born in
the cadre from the date of his initial appointment and
not after completion of training or probation."
20. Since, in the facts of the present case, as per
the Office Memorandum dated 31.03.2001 - Annexure 4,
till the new regulations were framed, the Uttarakhand
Power Corporation Ltd. was to follow the Regulations of
1970 and 1998 of the U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. for the
purpose of recruitment and fixation of seniority. It is not
the case of the respondents that any new Regulations
have been framed by the Uttarakhand Power Corporation
Ltd. Hence, for all intents and purposes, as per the Office
Memorandum dated 31.03.2001, the seniority Rules of
the U.P. Power Corporation Ltd., i.e. the 1970 Regulations
and 1998 Regulations, have to be followed, and the Rule
of seniority, which is Rule 19 reproduced above, is very

18
clear that the seniority has to be fixed from the date a
selected candidate joins on the post. Hence, for all
intents and purposes, the training period cannot be
deleted once an Assistant Engineer, after due selection
process, has joined the cadre.
21. Another fact, which can be highlighted, is that
even if during service any employee is sent for further
training, that period cannot be deleted from his seniority.
It is part of his service, and at the initial stage if he is
given training, or even after ten years he is sent for
training, that period of training has to be part of his
regular service record.
22. In view of the above discussion, the present
Writ Petitions are being allowed. The order of the
Tribunal is being set-aside. A direction is being given to
the Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd. to fix the
seniority after giving the benefit of seniority to all the
Assistant Engineers, who joined in the year 2006-07,
2007-08 & 2008-09 from the date of their joining the
department, and keeping in view the rota quota between
the direct recruits and the promotees. The entire
exercise shall be completed with a period of eight weeks

19
from the date of production of a certified copy of this
judgment.
23. Pending application(s), if any, also stand
disposed of accordingly.
